_about: Academic values of the Speaking marking, read by services/ai/speaking_grader.py and scripts/speaking_regression.py. Owned by the academic lead: change a value here, not in the code.

accepted._about: Spoken wordings the academic lead ruled no mistake (2026-10-29, the Part 3 travel report): a flag on one of them is set aside whatever the mistake filter says. "daily lifestyles" was self-corrected to "routines" in the recording, but the transcript drops the correction, so the self-correction check can't see it.

short_sample._about: 2026-11-11: one-question checks (20-40 s, 40-90 words) came out 6.0-7.0 for 8.5-9 speakers. Under this many spoken words a check is a short sample: its report says the band is approximate and its feedback is capped at 12k tokens.
short_sample._scoring_rules: true: the scoring runs are told brevity is no Lexical Resource or Grammar reason, and the mistake density is counted over at least 'words' words. Switched OFF 2026-11-11 after the teachers' six checks: it lifted #38 6.5 -> 8.0 and #39 7.0 -> 9.0 (the teachers: 6.5 and 7.0) - with little to quote, the weakness lists came back empty and 8 became 9. The official 9.0 recording's single answers did rise (85 words 6.5 -> 8.0). Measure on the teachers' checks before switching it on again.
short_sample._no_floor: Tried and dropped the same day: a no-mistake floor of 8 for a short sample lifted a basic answer ('It is fun. We eat good food.', rightly Lexical 5 / Grammar 5) to 7.0 - no mistake is not a wide range.

pronunciation_bands._about: Pronunciation from Azure's measurement (services/ai/pronunciation.py): the accuracy band, which a lower prosody band takes down by prosody_max_drop at most (never up); each band the first [least score, band] it reaches; accuracy alone when prosody isn't returned. Calibrated 2026-11-11 on the teachers' six checks (#38-43, Pronunciation 6, 6, 5, 6, 8, 8): their 8s had accuracy 99 and prosody 86-88, their 6s accuracy 93-94 and prosody 78-80, their 5 prosody 73 - 6 of 6 match. 2026-11-13: Azure's prosody falls with every pause and filler (#77 53, #80 68, #81 72 with fluency 59, 73, 68), so as the lower of the two bands it took hesitant speakers with clear words (accuracy 90-95) to Pronunciation 4-5 - hesitation is Fluency's. Re-check with more teacher-marked checks.

anchors._about: Recordings with the bands certified examiners gave them, shown to every scoring run (transcripts in data/calibration/speaking_anchors.json, on the server only - never in a report). real9-p3-travel: a candidate with an official 9.0 (Speaking 9.0), Part 3, six travel questions - added by the academic lead on 2026-10-27. teachers-sNN: checks #NN with our IELTS teachers' band for each criterion (2026-11-13, the user's OK): on these 11 checks the scoring runs were 0.55-0.65 of a band under the teachers on Lexical and Grammar, and 1.5 under on short answers of strong speakers (#42, #79) - the teachers' own marking is the standard. Add more teacher-marked checks as they come; test a check against the others (exclude_anchor).

regression._about: Expected results of scripts/speaking_regression.py (recordings in data/calibration/speaking/<id>/). A recording that is also an anchor is tested without itself as an anchor - otherwise the test would only show the anchor back.

real9-p3-travel._single: 2026-11-11: each answer of the official 9.0 recording marked on its own (--single), as a one-question check is; teachers saw 8.5-9 speakers get 6.5-7 on such checks.
